append_lessons.scope: Extends quarter/sparse evidence with one H100 M8 early-load screen and same-seed5344 package fixed-body trial. Initial +0.192us paired/+0.160us F1 becomes package +0.031999us paired/+0.176000us F1, but package paired mean -0.033333us and order medians +0.096000/-0.192000us. M1 keyed package separately loses -0.048000us paired/-0.960001us F1. No independent fixture or official transfer claim.
transfer_limits: Quarter native first-MMA PRMT16 to4; sparse nonNOP462 to455 are static changes, not runtime savings.
Profile durations22400/21664/21984ns are not gains; profile ranking opposes clean timings.
Counters do not identify repair PC time, wall-time fractions or a proven bottleneck.
A losing version does not reject quarter/pipeline family; preserve mixed F1 and negative paired estimates.
Earlier native issue is realized; reduced hardware wait was not measured for this binary. Prior quarter/sparse counters do not attribute early-load cause.
Binary placement, run order, clocks and residual timing variation remain possible transfer factors; none is identified as the cause.
Prior quarter/sparse and early-load jobs differ in weights and event handling; their difference is not a controlled causal contrast.
The old earlier-first-MMA sufficiency refutation is scoped to quarter/sparse, not all load/decode pipelining.
append_lessons.falsification: Next implementation hypothesis: move only next-W loads early while leaving next-X issue unchanged, eliminating the X snapshot/live range. Compare parent, current W+X early-load and W-only at the same selected M8 tuple and same stored W/X, retain both pair orders and F1 endpoints. If W-only loses while W+X wins, W-only sufficiency is refuted; if W-only wins with reduced native copy/live-range cost, pursue that narrower schedule. No unchanged rerun or new profiling gate.
